text:
marta: Heads-up — post-RFC follow-up. We merged the endpoint-affinity RFC; want a short sync about tenant proxy affinity + egress-window tradeoffs (shared regional proxy vs per-tenant private endpoints). Who's around?

kevin: SG. Quick summary: shared regional proxy lowers ENI/NAT cost and ops overhead but increases blast radius and makes source-IP preservation harder. Per-tenant endpoints give isolation and clean IPs but are expensive at scale.

ashley: We saw SNAT port pressure in prod last week on one AZ — peaked ~80% port allocation for a handful of heavy tenants. Not theoretical.

sam: ack. Can someone paste the affinity config we're considering?

marta: here's the minimal idea we sketched in the RFC notes:
```
route:
  affinity_ttl: 60s  # keep client->backend affinity for short-lived sessions
  fallback: regional-proxy
  backoff_policy: exponential
```

jun: Short affinity TTL reduces KV cache hit rate on the model-serving side -> latency climbs. If affinity TTL < user session length, we lose prefix cache benefits.

ashley: Also: per-tenant endpoints simplifies enterprise compliance (dedicated private IPs, easier cert pinning) — customers on Private plan ask for that.

kevin: Cost sketch (very rough): assume 1 ENI per endpoint, 1000 tenants -> infeasible. But we can do ENI sharing inside tenant groups or use regional NAT gateway pooling to reduce per-tenant IPs. Still, ops complexity increases.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: RFC #312 (endpoint-affinity) merged to main. CI ✅

sam: proposal: hybrid approach. Default = shared regional proxy for self-serve / low-tier customers. Enterprise = per-tenant private endpoint + static egress IPs. Add an "egress_preserve" token for customers that need source-ip preservation and route them to per-tenant path.

marta: hybrid seems pragmatic. Need checklist: latency impact, cost delta, port exhaustion safety, rollout plan, security/PKI changes.

ashley: I'll run an experiment in staging: synthetic load with short/long affinity TTLs plus a replay of sampled prod traffic to measure SNAT port use and tail latency. Target deliverable: numbers + ops playbook. I can do this by Thursday. :thumbsup: 

kevin: I'll build a quick cost model (ENIs, NATs, per-tenant infra vs shared). Will drop spreadsheet link here when ready: https://go/really-real-costs (placeholder)

jun: If we go hybrid we need a clear control-plane contract: how the control plane advertises route preference, how we flip a tenant from shared->dedicated, and a canary/rollout plan for DNS + peering. I can draft the contract.

marta: action items recap: 1) ashley: staging spike (latency + SNAT numbers) 2) kevin: cost model 3) jun: control-plane contract + rollout plan 4) sam: design doc snippet for egress_preserve token + feature flag. We'll reconvene Fri 10am PT.

ashley: volunteering for 1. I'll attach test harness and results in #eng-runtime when done.

kevin: volunteering for 2. Will include sensitivity to tenancy count and ENI pooling heuristics.

sam: I'll write the egress_preserve proposal + perms mapping. Also think about supporting a transitional mode: shared proxy but reserved source IPs via per-tenant NAT mapping.

jun: I'll start the control-plane contract doc and include sequence diagrams for flip-over and rollback (DNS TTLs, peering update steps).

marta: sweet. If anyone hits blockers or needs customer context, ping me or drop the tenant IDs. Otherwise see you Fri 10.

kevin: minor note — we should surface this in the Console roadmap because routing choices affect costs shown to customers.

ashley: noted. I'll include a short blurb for Product.

infra-bot: reminder: weekly-networking-ops sync tomorrow 09:30 PT.

marta: thanks all.
